rows.label: R01
rows.description: Cross-team coordination latency can propagate delays when dependencies are not surfaced early in planning cycles.

rows.label: R02
rows.description: Approval queues become unstable under concurrent initiatives unless reviewers are shielded with capacity buffers.

rows.label: R03
rows.description: Data anomalies require clear triage ownership and escalation criteria to avoid unresolved quality debt.

rows.label: R04
rows.description: Support readiness depends on localized documentation consistency and scenario-based training coverage.

rows.label: R05
rows.description: Release governance quality improves when gate criteria are measurable and reviewed with consistent cadence.

rows.label: R06
rows.description: Monitoring thresholds should be tuned iteratively to preserve true-signal value and reduce noisy alerts.

rows.label: R07
rows.description: Incident drills expose ownership ambiguity that should be corrected before critical launch windows.

rows.label: R08
rows.description: Operational metrics interpretation can diverge without shared KPI definitions for edge-case handling.

rows.label: R09
rows.description: Escalation speed improves when decision logs are accessible and updated near real time by accountable owners.

rows.label: R10
rows.description: Mitigation plans need measurable leading indicators to support steering decisions in weekly reviews.

rows.label: R11
rows.description: Capacity bottlenecks in specialist reviews should be anticipated with fallback approval sequencing.

rows.label: R12
rows.description: Service stability is reinforced by repeatability in runbooks and post-incident action tracking.

rows.label: R13
rows.description: Execution variance decreases when dependencies are modeled explicitly across all active workstreams.

rows.label: R14
rows.description: Readiness confidence increases when pre-launch checklists map clearly to accountable roles and timelines.
